subject: Post-demo follow-up: DPA scope, residency, and logging questions from HearthHealth
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: DPA scope, residency, and logging questions from HearthHealth

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the candid feedback. As promised, a short written recap with the privacy/data handling points we flagged and next steps so your legal/procurement folks have something concrete to work from.

Key items you asked about:
- Controller vs. Processor: Redwood serves as a processor for hosted/Dedicated deployments; you (HearthHealth) would be the controller for customer-provided data. We can accept processor-side obligations in the addendum where required (see draft attached).
- Subprocessors: we maintain a current list; I attached the latest CSV. We also publish a dynamic list and notify customers per the DPA when new subprocessors are added.
- Breach notification: we typically commit to notify customers without undue delay and in practice provide an initial notification within 72 hours of becoming aware for incidents involving customer data — legal can propose alternate windows during redlines.
- Data residency: Hosted EU region (Frankfurt) available for tenant isolation. Dedicated/Private deployments also possible if you need VPC or on-prem.
- Logs & retention: platform audit logs retained by default for 13 months; we can configure shorter retention (e.g., 12 months) or export logs to your storage for arbitrary retention policies.
- PII handling: support for redaction/pseudonymization in pipelines and end-to-end encryption in transit and at rest (AES-256). KMS integration supported for Dedicated/Private.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Draft.pdf (redlineable), DPA_questions.xlsx (your worksheet to capture asks), subprocessor_list_20270424.csv (current subprocessors).

Next steps I propose:
1) Your team to confirm the must-have DPA clauses (controller obligations you need us to accept) and any non-starters in DPA_questions.xlsx.
2) Redwood legal (cc Marissa) to send a clean DPA + redline timeline by EOD Mon 4/26.
3) We’ll provide SOC2 Type II evidence and the signed subprocessor attestations via secure link once procurement requests them.

If procurement needs a single point of contact, please loop procurement@hearthhealth.com and Ben (cc’d) — he can handle technical evidence and the subprocessor Q&A.

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0191

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: DPA scope, residency, and logging questions from HearthHealth

Thanks Aisha — this is helpful and exactly what procurement/legal asked for. A few clarifying questions before we start redlines: 

1) Controller/processor: You say Redwood is the processor — can you confirm there are no circumstances where Redwood would classify as a controller for provisioning/telemetry data (e.g., anonymized usage metrics)? We need clarity for our compliance team.

2) Subprocessor notice: What is your standard notification cadence (e.g., 30 days prior)? Do you allow customers to object to a new subprocessor and, if so, what is the escalation path?

3) Breach notice timing: Procurement has a hard requirement for "initial notification within 48 hours" for anything deemed a security incident affecting PII. Is Redwood willing to commit to 48 hours in the DPA or do you require 72?

4) Residency & segregation: We need assurance that all data and associated logs for our tenant remain physically within EU data centers (Frankfurt) for the hosted option. If you fallback to other regions for capacity, we need automatic failover to a compatible EU region only.

5) Logs retention: Our policy requires 12 months of immutable audit logs for user access and admin actions. Can you export immutably to our S3 bucket or provide a retention configuration?

Procurement would like the DPA fully executed by May 10 if possible — can you confirm you have resources for that timeline?

Best,
Sarah Linden
Head of Compliance
HearthHealth
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Linden <sarah.linden@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: DPA scope, residency, and logging questions from HearthHealth

Hi Sarah — quick answers inline and next-step commitments. Marissa (legal) is cc’d and will own the formal DPA/redline exchange.

> 1) Controller/processor: You say Redwood is the processor — can you confirm there are no circumstances where Redwood would classify as a controller for provisioning/telemetry data (e.g., anonymized usage metrics)?
We act as a processor with respect to customer-provided content and PII. For anonymized/aggregate telemetry that is derived and not tied to a customer identifier, we treat it as platform telemetry for product ops; that data is handled under our privacy policy. If you require contractual constraints on telemetry-derived datasets, we can add a clause to the DPA to limit use and require anonymization thresholds.

> 2) Subprocessor notice: What is your standard notification cadence (e.g., 30 days prior)? Do you allow customers to object to a new subprocessor and, if so, what is the escalation path?
Standard: we notify customers at least 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor and publish the list. If a customer objects on reasonable grounds, we will engage to either (a) delay onboarding until mitigation is in place, (b) offer a compatible alternative (Dedicated/Private), or (c) help with technical compensating controls. Legal will include the formal objection process in the DPA.

> 3) Breach notice timing: Procurement has a hard requirement for "initial notification within 48 hours" for anything deemed a security incident affecting PII. Is Redwood willing to commit to 48 hours in the DPA or do you require 72?
We prefer an initial notification window of 72 hours for incidents that require investigation to determine scope. That said, I will escalate to security/legal to see if we can sign to 48 hours for high-severity incidents — Marissa will advise in the redline.

> 4) Residency & segregation: We need assurance that all data and associated logs for our tenant remain physically within EU data centers (Frankfurt) for the hosted option. If you fallback to other regions for capacity, we need automatic failover to a compatible EU region only.
Confirmed: we can pin your tenant to the eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) region for hosted. Our smart routing/fallback can be constrained by policy to EU-only regions; Ben can confirm the exact behavior for cross-region fallback.

> 5) Logs retention: Our policy requires 12 months of immutable audit logs for user access and admin actions. Can you export immutably to our S3 bucket or provide a retention configuration?
Yes — we offer log export to customer-owned S3 (or Azure Blob) with object lock capabilities to enable immutability for the retention period you specify. Alternatively, we can set the platform retention to 12 months for those event types. Ben will follow up with the export details and an example lifecycle policy.

Timeline: we can aim to have an initial DPA redline and SOC2 evidence link by end-of-day Mon 4/26; if that works for procurement, we should be able to meet a May 10 execution target assuming standard review cycles.

Next steps (owners):
- Marissa (legal) to share clean DPA + comments by 4/26 (owner: Marissa).
- Ben to share S3 export guidance and confirm region-fallback policy (owner: Ben) by EOD 4/26.
- Aisha to consolidate procurement asks and schedule follow-up call if needed (owner: Aisha).

Thanks — will follow up with attachments/links shortly.

Aisha

Hi Sarah — Ben here from Solutions/Platform. A few technical clarifications to back up Aisha's notes: 

- Residency: For hosted tenants we use eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) region. We can pin compute and storage to that region and set routing policy to EU-only. Automatic scaling will stay in-region; cross-region failover only happens under extreme conditions and can be disabled.

- Encryption/KMS: All customer objects are encrypted at rest (AES-256). For Dedicated or Private you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS integration; we also support HSM-backed keys for high-compliance customers.

- Logs: We can stream audit and admin logs to your S3 with an example CloudFormation policy. For immutable retention we recommend S3 Object Lock + retention via lifecycle lock. I attached the current subprocessor CSV (subprocessor_list_20270424.csv) and an export example.

- Telemetry: platform telemetry (aggregate usage) is stored separately and can be disabled for your tenant on request.

If you want, I can run a short technical session with your security architect to confirm export configuration and region pinning — I have availability Wed 4/28 10:00-11:00 CET.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
